subject.title: RFC 0026: Automations terminology and configurable feature naming

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed two-stage direction: a model-visible runtime rename from cron to Automations with a bounded compatibility alias, followed by locale-aware configurable terminology shared by Control UI, prompts, and post-bootstrap CLI output?
rationale: This RFC deliberately introduces new product and configuration surface across several owners; no mechanical review outcome can determine whether the terminology direction and broadened `ui` contract should become a supported product commitment.

options.title: Approve staged direction
options.body: Approve Phase 1 with the stated identity-migration contract and require Phase 2 to land only through the accepted localization owner gates.

options.title: Approve terminology only
options.body: Accept the canonical Automations terminology sweep but defer configurable custom naming until a narrower runtime-language configuration contract is sponsored.

options.title: Keep cron as runtime identity
options.body: Retain cron as the agent-tool identity and pursue presentation-only wording if maintainers do not want a compatibility alias and migration window.

recommendation.title: Approve staged direction
recommendation.body: Approve Phase 1 with the stated identity-migration contract and require Phase 2 to land only through the accepted localization owner gates.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the accepted related localization RFC and performed the detailed compatibility review that the current proposal addresses.
